text:
sam_support: Heads-up — incoming P1 from Acme (ticket #5421). Their streaming chat + tool/function calling flow intermittently emits malformed structured output, breaking their webhook parser. They say it started after our last runtime patch. https://acme.atlassian/5421

maria_sales: Ugh. Acme is on Dedicated in us-west and says it's blocking a live rollout. They want a patch + clear rollback plan.

linda_product: Can you paste a sample failing stream and the parser error? Need to know whether this is framing (chunk boundaries) or function-call json body shape.

sam_support: Pasted excerpt from their logs: ```
STREAM_FRAME: {"type":"tool_event","name":"send_email","payload":"{\"to\":\"x@acme.com\",\"body\":\"Hi\"}"}
STREAM_FRAME: {"type":"tool_event","name":"send_email","payload\":"{\"to\":\"x@acme.com\",\"body\":\"Hi\"}\""}
// note the missing closing brace in one frame, then next frame is valid -> parser chokes
```

raj_eng: Quick glance: looks like the chunker can sometimes emit partial JSON frames when fncall events interleave with streaming deltas. Probably a race in the stream emitter when flush/kvcache events coincide.

linda_product: Options we can take:
A) Immediate bugfix in chunker (longer dev + QA)
B) Hotfix: add an opt-in compatibility header so clients can request atomic frames (server ensures each stream chunk contains complete JSON objects)
C) Docs + SDK guidance for resilient parsers (longer-term).

maria_sales: Acme wants B + hotfix. They need something quick they can flip on while we work the deeper fix.

emma_pm: Need a decision by EOD to schedule a hotfix this week. If we go with B, define launch criteria: tests, staging signoff, canary, and docs snippet. Also estimate eng effort.

raj_eng: Rough estimates: B (compat header + server-side atomicization) = ~2 dev-days + 1 day QA + 0.5 day staging/canary rollout. A (chunker root cause) is more like 5-8 dev-days plus deeper regression coverage.

linda_product: Proposed launch criteria for B (hotfix):
- unit tests covering interleaved fncall/stream scenarios
- integration test with streaming SDK verifying atomic frames
- Acme validation on staging (their parser must succeed)
- Canary @ 10% traffic with monitoring for errors for 6 hours
- Rollback header/flag to disable at runtime if issues

ops-bot: deploy-window-check: available tonight 23:00 PDT -> maintenance_window: yes

sam_support: I'll get Acme to run their parser against staging once you provide the endpoint and the header name. Their engineer is available 21:00 PDT.

maria_sales: I'll push for the staging test and confirm we get the green from the customer before canary.

linda_product: Decision: proceed with B as the immediate hotfix and schedule A for next sprint to remove the compatibility shim. @raj_eng can you assign?

raj_eng: Assigning to kai_eng. Creating issue: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/9876 — title: "opt-in: atomic streaming frames header (hotfix)". ETA: start tonight, target deploy tomorrow morning Canary.

kai_eng: Taking it. Plan: add header X-Redwood-Atomic-Frames: true -> server will buffer until a full JSON object boundary detected before emitting frame. Will add unit + e2e tests. Will ping when staging endpoint is ready.

emma_pm: I'll own the rollout checklist and acceptance criteria. Once Acme verifies staging, we proceed with 10% canary. If canary is clean for 6 hours we promote. If not, rollback using the header toggle.

sam_support: Thanks — keeping ticket #5421 updated. I'll post Acme's staging feedback here.

maria_sales: Appreciate the quick triage. Also let's prep a short customer note explaining the compatibility header and our timeline.

linda_product: Agreed. I'll draft the customer note after Kai confirms staging endpoint.

ops-bot: deploy-plan-created: https://deploys.internal/plan/67321

raj_eng: Follow-up: ticket added to sprint board under "hotfixes" and "streaming" lanes.

kai_eng: Starting work now. Will update with PR and staging URL when ready.

sam_support: ACK, standing by for staging link.
